findings.title: Post-schedule DB failure is counted as SMS scheduling failure
findings.body: The catch block wraps both `twilio.scheduleSMS` and the subsequent `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that marks the reminder as scheduled. If Twilio successfully schedules the SMS but the DB update fails (transient DB error, unique `referenceId` conflict, etc.), the code increments `retryCount` as if the SMS scheduling failed. The reminder remains `scheduled: false`, so the next cron run will schedule the same SMS again, causing duplicate messages. After two such failures the reminder is deleted even though an SMS is already scheduled on Twilio. The retry count should only be incremented for failures from the actual scheduling call, not for failures while updating the result record.

findings.title: Retry-based deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new OR branch deletes every `WorkflowReminder` whose `retryCount` is greater than 1, without filtering by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`. Although this PR currently only increments `retryCount` for SMS reminders, `retryCount` is a column on the shared `WorkflowReminder` model, so EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders could be silently deleted if they ever have `retryCount > 1`. The condition should include `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and probably `scheduled: false` to avoid deleting valid reminders for other methods.

findings.title: Missing sendTo or empty message never increments retry count
findings.body: The retry count is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` is actually called and fails or throws. If `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing/falsy, the reminder is skipped entirely, remains `scheduled: false`, and retains the same `retryCount`. Such reminders will be selected forever on every cron run, which is the exact repeated-scheduling problem this PR is meant to fix. Missing or invalid recipient data should also count as a failed attempt or otherwise remove the reminder.

findings.title: retryCount update is not atomic and can lose failures under concurrent runs
findings.body: Both failure paths set `retryCount` to `reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value fetched at the start of the handler. If this endpoint is invoked concurrently by overlapping cron runs, two attempts can both read `retryCount: 0` and both write `retryCount: 1`, so two failures are counted as one. The reminder may then be retried indefinitely instead of deleted after two failures. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of setting it from the stale value.
